runnerProcessFailure.note: a same-host monitor/container can prove process death by injection (SIGKILL + heartbeat staleness); this capability is real and may be marked complete at process level.

runnerHostFailure.note: proving host-down detection within 2 minutes requires a monitoring instance outside the Runner fault domain; a monitor that dies with the host can never prove it.

rules.note: when the co-hosted monitor stops with the host, the fault domain must be marked NOT satisfied — never PASS; failure of the monitoring system itself must be discovered by the existing platform monitoring, and an unregistered monitor keeps the admission gap open.

alertAuditPersistence.note: alert delivery audit lives outside the Runner backup domain so a Runner volume failure cannot destroy all alert evidence.
